name: Balsamic Roast
ingredients: 3 or 4 lb - meat. Any cut of lamb or beef works well with this recipe
1 cup - dry red wine (we freeze leftover wine just for this purpose!)
3-4 cup - beef stock (1 cup per lb meat). Don’t skimp!
instructions: Prepare the pan: select a casserole or roasting pan with a lid that just fits the size of meat you are cooking. If it doesn’t seal well, line the pan with tin foil.
Season the meat: Salt and pepper liberally. Set aside.

Cook the veggies: In casserole dish or a medium frying pan, add oil, onions and carrots. Cook until veggies are caramelized and golden brown. Onions will reduce dramatically. It takes at least 10 minutes. Reduce heat to low. Add garlic. Stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Remove from pan and set aside.
Deglaze pan: Add wine and vinegar to pan. Stir well, scraping up the yummy bits.
Add all other ingredients to casserole dish: meat, veggies, stock, thyme and bay leaf
Cook: cover with tight fitting lid or seal with tin foil. Bake for 2-3 hours until meat is very tender. Check part way through and add more water or stock if liquid has evaporated.
Testing for tender: Fork inserted in the meat should slide in and out. It will ‘stick’ if the meat is not tender enough.

Serve: strain the onions and carrots out of the sauce and serve in a side dish. Put meat on a serving dish. Cover and keep warm in a low oven. Put the liquid in a gravy pitcher and spoon off or remove excess fat. You could serve as is or reduce in a sauce pan or thicken like a gravy.

additional_context.source: Adapted from Leslie Stowes Balsamic Short Ribs.
additional_context.tips: Suggested sides: Great with wild rice, lentils, barley or mashed potatoes. Sautéed spinach with a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper is nice as are pan fried carrots or roasted root vegetables. If you choose to have a salad, keep the salad dressing and flavours mild – the balsamic vinegar in the meat makes for a flavourful sauce. You can freeze what you don’t eat.
